subject: Civil Engineering
title: Ultra-High-Performance Concrete
description: A quick, practical guide to Ultra-High-Performance Concrete.

hook.text: Normal concrete handles 4,000 psi. UHPC reaches 29,000 psi — stronger than some steel.

buildup.text: UHPC uses no coarse aggregate — only fine sand, cement, silica fume, and steel fibers.

discovery.text: The water-cement ratio is below 0.25 — almost every particle reacts, leaving no pores.

twist.text: UHPC is ductile — steel fibers give it tensile capacity. It bends instead of shattering.

climax.text: Bridge deck joints and protective cladding panels are early UHPC applications.

punchline.text: Concrete that bends like metal and lasts like stone — that's the new frontier.

quiz.question: What makes UHPC fundamentally different from normal concrete?
options: It uses plastic aggregate instead of stone
No coarse aggregate, ultra-low w/c ratio, and steel fibers give it extreme strength and ductility
It is mixed with rubber to absorb impact energy
